sections.heading: Rules source
sections.supplies: The file holding this project's rules for agents, and any file that merely points at it.
sections.fallback: Skills look for AGENTS.md then CLAUDE.md at the repo root, and say in their report that they guessed.

sections.heading: Repo
sections.supplies: owner/repo, visibility, and the collaborator model (single maintainer or a team).
sections.fallback: owner/repo is derived from the git remote. Without a stated collaborator model, review-sweep requires an APPROVED review and will not use the reaction-count shortcut.

sections.heading: Mechanical checks
sections.supplies: The commands that must pass before a push, one per line, most important first. Write 'none' if the project has no automated checks.
sections.fallback: pr-preflight reports that it ran no mechanical gate, which is a finding in itself. review-sweep pushes a review fix without the project gate and must say so in the PR thread. dependency-refresh runs whatever checks it can discover to decide whether a bump actually works, and reports that those were not the project's stated gate.

sections.heading: Derived docs
sections.supplies: A table of canonical file to the files that restate what it says, so a change to a fact can be traced to every copy of it. Note which dependents a reader acts on outside the repo. Write 'none' if no doc restates another.
sections.fallback: Docs currency covers the rules source, the profile and the vendored skills only, and a human-facing doc quoting a changed fact goes stale silently.

sections.heading: Dependencies
sections.supplies: Which manifests and lockfiles are authoritative, which ecosystems are in play, what is deliberately pinned and why, and the project's update policy.
sections.fallback: dependency-refresh discovers manifests by scanning, cannot tell a deliberate pin from a stale one, and reports every pin it could not classify. security-review reads it too: without it the supply-chain group falls back to scanning, must name which ecosystems it audited, and cannot tell a pin held deliberately from one forgotten. Reachability is unaffected — that comes from tracing repository usage under ci-workflows C5, not from this section.

sections.heading: Review focus
sections.supplies: This project's known failure modes: invariants that are easy to break, generated files that must not be hand-edited, conventions a reviewer should weight heavily.
sections.fallback: Reviews run the generic passes only and flag nothing project-specific.

sections.heading: Not findings
sections.supplies: Classes of feedback this project never wants raised, each with the reason. This is what lets a reviewer decline a recurring objection without re-arguing it.
sections.fallback: Only the skill's built-in not-findings list applies.

sections.heading: Local skills
sections.supplies: Skills that live only in this repo and what each one gates, so a shared skill can hand off to them. Write 'none' if there are none.
sections.fallback: No hand-off; pr-preflight runs only the vendored skills.

sections.heading: Exemptions
sections.supplies: Carve-outs, each naming the skill it applies to and why. Use for things that look like a violation but are not.
sections.fallback: No carve-outs; expect false positives where a project convention diverges from the generic rule.

sections.heading: Ship
sections.supplies: How this project pushes and opens PRs: branch naming, draft or not, which tooling to use, what to do after opening.
sections.fallback: Push the branch and open a draft PR with whatever GitHub tooling the session has.

sections.heading: Threat model
sections.supplies: One paragraph: what ships to parties you do not control, and what the single real control is that keeps one user out of another's data.
sections.fallback: security-review cannot rank findings by what actually matters here and will say so.

sections.heading: Trust boundary
sections.supplies: A table of path glob to check groups. This is the authoritative trigger list: a changed path matching a row runs that row's groups. Groups are authorization, auth-session, secrets, client-data, supply-chain, release.
sections.fallback: security-review runs the secrets and supply-chain groups over the whole diff and reports every other group as not configured.

sections.heading: Stack
sections.supplies: Which reference modules apply, from the skill's references directory: postgres-rls, ci-workflows, mobile-release. List only what this project actually uses.
sections.fallback: No reference module loads and the review stays at the level of the generic checks.

sections.heading: Identity model
sections.supplies: How a user proves who they are, what key rows are owned by, and every redirect or deep-link surface that participates in auth.
sections.fallback: The auth-session group reports as not configured.

sections.heading: Secrets policy
sections.supplies: Which env prefixes are public by design, where real secrets live, and what must never appear in a commit.
sections.fallback: The secrets group flags only obvious credential patterns and cannot tell a public key from a private one.

sections.heading: Probe policy
sections.supplies: Whether live cross-account probing is permitted, against which environment, with which accounts, and what is off limits. Write 'no live probing' to forbid it.
sections.fallback: No live probing. Authorization findings rest on reading policy definitions only, which the report must state.

sections.heading: Known gaps
sections.supplies: Security findings already recorded, each with a status (open, accepted, launch blocker) so a review reports them as known rather than as new. Write 'none' when there are none.
sections.fallback: Every recurring finding is re-reported as new on each review, which trains the reader to skim them.

sections.heading: Release targets
sections.supplies: Where this project ships: app stores, a web deploy, a package registry, or none. Drives the release-readiness group.
sections.fallback: The release group is skipped and reported as skipped.
